title: Per-view navball
summary: Optional attitude instrument using the shared HUD lifecycle.

blocks.text: This module provides a flight attitude and velocity vector navball instrument rendered as vector overlay primitives. It displays ship pitch, heading, roll, prograde, retrograde, normal, anti-normal, radial, anti-radial, and maneuver target vectors across orbital and rotating surface reference frames without modifying flight mechanics.

items: Provides hud.navball@1.0.0 through the NAVBALL_HUD service key: provides the navball HudInstrumentDefinition for ViewHud hosting.
Fills the hud.navball slot in presentation profiles.
Requires no external services in its module manifest.
frame (default 0, from 0 to 2, step 1): Velocity reference frame mode: 0 automatically selects surface or orbital frame, 1 forces orbital frame, and 2 forces rotating surface frame.
orientation (default 0, from 0 to 1, step 1): Attitude dial orientation: 0 keeps local horizon upright, 1 rotates dial with camera orientation.
minimumSpeed (default 0.05, from 0 to 10, step 0.01): Direction marker noise floor in metres per second. Hides prograde/retrograde markers below this speed without modifying physics.
Initialization captures frame, orientation, and minimumSpeed settings, contributes this guide, and provides NAVBALL_HUD.
The instrument creates per-view instances using FLIGHT_HUD_STATE adapters supplied by the HUD context.
draw(into) samples ship attitude, velocity vectors, and maneuver nodes, pushing vector overlay circles, crosshairs, and markers into the overlay buffer.
dispose clears cached frame references and releases gesture bindings.

blocks.text: To replace attitude indicator styling, implement hud.navball@1.0.0 in the hud.navball slot. Removing this module omits the spherical navball dial from HUD views while leaving other telemetry instruments active.

Module version 0.1.0 uses API space-sim-game-api/2 and manifest format space-sim-module/2. Both are pre-freeze: attitude projection algorithms and marker drawing contracts may evolve prior to final API freeze.
examples/modules/navball demonstrates creating a navball instrument instance and rendering attitude vector overlays. Build and validate it from the repository root:

npm run module:build -- examples/modules/navball/module.json /tmp/example-navball.spacemod
npm run module:validate -- /tmp/example-navball.spacemod
